in_text_mentions: ined. The mother commented that her third child had a cleft lip and palate, so she had a pretty good idea of what to expect. She seemed to accept the situation well. She went into labor at 36 weeks and one day of pregnancy, and a vaginal delivery was performed on the same day. The baby was a 2,164 g boy with an Apgar score of 8/9. The hard palate was absent, resulting in a direct connection between the nasal and oral cavities. Additionally, the alveolar ridge was separated on both sides in the anterior portion of the maxilla, leading to a diagnosis of bilateral cleft lip and palate (Figure 3).
